findings.title: Activity/reference authority is a mutable self-hashed file
findings.evidence: The only worker, queue, service, KEEP and ACTIVE source is activity.json. Its hash authenticates only the file's current contents; a same-inode in-place rewrite with a recomputed hash is accepted. Each of workers, queues, services, keep and active refused while containing the entry and then retired after the reference was erased. No real worker/queue/service registry source is opened or bound to the entry generation.
findings.impact: A caller with the Store-owned file access can erase lifecycle references without changing the owner inode, and the empty default activity source can authorize an entry without an authoritative external audit.
findings.required_fix: Bind retirement to actual Store-owned worker/queue/service/lease/registry state, or refuse when that source is unavailable. A self-asserted JSON audit/hash is not sufficient evidence.

findings.title: Process cwd/fd/cmdline admission remains open after the final scan
findings.evidence: A private hook started a process only after the third process scan, the scan inside _delete_owned, returned. Separate cwd, open-fd and cmdline fixtures all returned retired and deleted the quarantined entry; scan count was three in each case.
findings.impact: A live process reference can be admitted between the last audit and destructive deletion. Repeated process scans are not exclusive admission.
findings.required_fix: Use a real supported exclusion/admission guard that covers process cwd/fd/cmdline references through deletion, or refuse with UNAPPLIED when no such guard exists.

findings.title: Lifecycle marker and activity races after audit are not closed
findings.evidence: A private checkpoint created KEEP after the quarantine marker audit and final process scan; retirement still returned retired and removed KEEP during ordinary deletion. A private quarantine hook added a valid self-hashed worker reference after _retirement_audit; retirement still returned retired.
findings.impact: A late KEEP/ACTIVE or lifecycle reference can be introduced after admission checks and is then ignored or deleted.
findings.required_fix: Make marker/reference state part of an exclusive Store-owned admission lease, revalidate under that guard immediately before deletion, and restore/refuse on any late change.

findings.title: Receipt validation does not prove node/sequence/registration association
findings.evidence: The strict malformed receipt matrix refused path, null node, string lock, string sequence, null/duplicate registration members, and null/duplicate suite members. However, a private receipt with a valid-shaped but wrong node, another retired entry's sequence, and another retired entry's registration was accepted by _load(). Node is type-checked but not tied to retirement history; registration membership is only checked against the global retired list.
findings.impact: Corrupted or cross-associated historical evidence can be accepted as authoritative despite passing the field/member-type checks.
findings.required_fix: Persist and validate exact retirement-history association for node, sequence, registrations and suites; reject valid-shaped but unrelated receipt values.

findings.title: Return evidence has a changed-source hash mismatch
findings.evidence: The return manifest records changed_source bench_store.py SHA-256 5af33a48e76c7cbd94ef2948d1b7bb6225a318bb0715762e98087b93c970b747. The exact candidate HEAD blob and worktree source both hash to 5504746d7348611878bb75128e20c1df22a9f237ad1b5a135fa40992c868758b; current mode is 0755.
findings.impact: The claimed source custody packet is not byte-exact for the reviewed candidate.
findings.required_fix: Regenerate the source manifest from the exact candidate commit/tree and recertify all dependent evidence before any installation.
